## Two kinds of tumour

Normal cells grow, age and die in a controlled manner. Sometimes this system breaks down, and abnormal cells start growing and dividing uncontrollably. The result is a tumour, which may be **benign** or **malignant**.

A benign tumour stays in one place. A malignant tumour is cancerous: it can invade nearby tissues and even spread to other parts of the body to form new tumours.
